vs_free_alternatives.coursera_andrew_ng: Andrew Ng covers ML theory well. Scaler differs in: (1) structured DSA + system design track specifically for SDE interviews, (2) live classes with direct Q&A vs recorded video, (3) 1:1 mentorship and accountability, (4) career support + hiring partner network, (5) cohort of serious peers — not self-paced isolation. Coursera won't mock-interview you or intro you to a hiring manager.
vs_free_alternatives.youtube_free_resources: Free resources require you to curate, sequence, and self-motivate. Scaler provides structured progression, accountability, and the peer pressure of a cohort moving together. The mentorship and placement network are what you cannot get for free.

general_scaler_facts.founded: 2019 by Abhimanyu Saxena and Anshuman Singh (ex-Facebook, ex-Directi)
general_scaler_facts.faculty_background: Engineers from Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Hotstar, Flipkart
general_scaler_facts.live_class_format: 3 live classes per week, highly interactive, recorded for replay
general_scaler_facts.mentorship: Bimonthly 1:1 sessions with industry veterans; mentors have helped thousands with interview prep and career guidance
general_scaler_facts.entrance_test: Scaler requires candidates to clear an entrance test before enrollment. It tests DSA and problem-solving fundamentals. Designed to ensure cohort quality — not to filter out motivated candidates.
general_scaler_facts.entrance_test_prep: Scaler provides preparation resources. The test is designed to be passable with focused effort — typically 2-4 weeks of structured prep. It's a signal of commitment, not a gatekeeping mechanism.
placement_support: Dedicated recruitment team that connects learners with hiring partners
Mock interviews with working professionals at target companies
Alumni referrals and warm intros to hiring managers
payment_options: No-cost EMI through NBFCs and bank partners
Income Share Agreement (ISA) option for eligible candidates
Scholarships available based on merit and financial need
Can start with as low as ₹9,791/month
general_scaler_facts.scaler_vs_college: College gives you a degree. Scaler gives you interview-ready skills. Most Tier-2/3 college placements are ₹3-4 LPA. Scaler alumni from similar backgrounds regularly land ₹8-15 LPA first roles.
general_scaler_facts.cohort_quality: Selective admissions ensure peers are equally serious. Average learner in a Scaler cohort has 2-3 years experience or a strong academic background. Senior cohorts (like those Karthik would join) include engineers from top product companies looking to go deeper on AI/system design.

common_objections_and_handles.price_too_high: The fee is ~₹3.5L. At 14 LPA today, a 50% hike to 21 LPA adds ₹7L+ per year. The program pays for itself in 6 months of salary delta. EMI makes it cash-flow neutral during the program itself.
common_objections_and_handles.coursera_free: Free resources don't mock-interview you, don't intro you to hiring managers, and don't hold you accountable. What you're paying for is the structure, the mentor network, and the placement engine — not the content.
common_objections_and_handles.am_i_too_late_for_ai: The shift to AI engineering is still early. The engineers who upskill in 2025-2026 will define the next 10 years. Waiting makes the gap wider, not smaller.
common_objections_and_handles.will_i_clear_entrance_test: The entrance test is designed to be passable with 2-4 weeks of focused prep. Scaler provides resources. It filters for commitment, not raw talent.
common_objections_and_handles.job_guarantee: Scaler doesn't offer a blanket guarantee, but 900+ hiring partners, dedicated placement teams, and alumni referrals create a support system. Alumni from similar profiles (Tier-2/3 colleges, 0 YoE) regularly land ₹8-12 LPA first roles in product companies.
common_objections_and_handles.worth_it_for_experienced: If you're at 14 LPA in services and want 25-35 LPA at a product company, the math works. The program is worth it if the outcome delta is real — and Scaler alumni data backs that up.
common_objections_and_handles.cohort_level: Scaler's selective admissions mean your cohort will challenge you. Senior tracks attract engineers from product companies who want to go deeper. You won't be tutoring beginners.
